newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins lower in speculative trade.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins lower in speculative trade.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds eased in speculative trading on Wednesday but dealers said the decline was small thanks to mainly foreign support, with prices likely to firm until Friday.
"Bullish and bearish trends are fighting on the market, while bid and offer spreads are quite tiny," Moscow Business World Bank dealer Sergei Kovzharov said.
An ICFI Moscow Partners Bank dealer said prices recovered later up to the open levels on short-covering after an early speculative fall.

Dealers said there was no impact on Minfins after Ukraine's parliament delayed ratification on Wednesday of a deal with Russia under which Kiev would renounce claims to Soviet assets in return for Moscow assuming Ukraine's share of Soviet foreign debt.
"It is Russia who is in charge of the Soviet debt now so its (postponement) should not worry London Club," Kovzharov said.
Dealers said prices were likely to firm this week, with main support seen among London and U.S. investors.
